sentences.text: The crime was registered against the Manager/Foreman of Chirala Branch of Margadarshi Chit Fund Private Limited (for brevity "MCFPL").
The Manager of Chirala Branch was arrested and remanded to judicial custody and thereafter he was enlarged on bail.

5. According to defacto complainant, her husband has been working in Railways and she came to know that there is a chit opened in the MCFPL of Chirala Branch in the name of her husband as subscriber and thereafter he became prized subscriber, and he did not withdraw the prize money.

The defacto complainant enquired her husband, who is in hospital, and came to know that her husband did not join as subscriber of chit, being organized by Chirala branch and his signatures were forged.
Based on the said complaint, the above crime was registered.

6. The 3rd respondent-Inspector of Police issued notice under Section 102 of Cr.P.C to 5th respondent, Branch Manager of the 4th Respondent-Bank to freeze 3 accounts of MCFPL with 4th respondent-Bank of Chirala Branch.
The 3rd SRSJ respondent served notice to Branch Manager on 22.09.2023.
On the same day, the 5th respondent through letter dated 22.09.2023 intimated to 3rd respondent that 3 accounts were totally freezed.
The bank also furnished a copy to the petitioners regarding freezing of accounts.
Aggrieved by the same, the above writ petition is filed.

7. Sri Naga Muthu, learned senior counsel for petitioners would submit that Chirala Branch/Foreman of the petitioners is overseeing 28 chit groups within the branch and there are total 1279 subscribers.
As of the date of freezing of accounts, total balance in the respective accounts is Rs.1,49,38,313/-.
Learned senior counsel would submit that as per Section 22 of the Chit Funds Act, 1982 (for short "the Act") two separate accounts must be opened in the Bank.
Account No.1 is to deposit monthly installment payments of subscribers and Account No.2 is to deposit prize chit amount that remains unclaimed or unpaid for 30 days.
As per Section 30 of the Act, a separate account needs to be opened.
Thus, a total of 3 accounts were opened and they are being operated.
SRSJ 8.
Learned senior counsel would submit that the amount payable to husband of defacto complainant is Rs.3,00,000/- and in fact, prized subscriber did not claim the money by producing sureties.
Due to freezing of accounts, the Foreman is unable to collect and deposit the monthly subscription amounts of 28 chit groups.

He would also submit that under Section 102 of Cr.P.C. bank account of a person can be freezed only when the transactions in the bank account have direct nexus with the offence alleged against the accused.
He would also submit that in the facts of the case, writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is maintainable.

sentences.text: Before answering the questions, we feel the urge to say a few words on the exercise of writ powers conferred by Article 226 of the Constitution having come across certain orders passed by the high courts holding writ petitions as "not maintainable" merely because the alternative remedy provided by the relevant statutes has not been pursued by the parties desirous of invocation of the writ jurisdiction.
The power to issue prerogative writs under Article 226 is plenary in nature.
Any limitation on the exercise of such power must be traceable in the Constitution itself.
Profitable reference in this regard may be made to Article 329 and ordainments of other similarly worded articles in the Constitution.
Article 226 does not, in terms, impose any limitation or restraint on the 2023 SCC OnLine SC 95 SRSJ exercise of power to issue writs.

While it is true that exercise of writ powers despite availability of a remedy under the very statute which has been invoked and has given rise to the action impugned in the writ petition ought not to be made in a routine manner, yet, the mere fact that the petitioner before the high court, in a given case,
has not pursued the alternative remedy available to him/it cannot mechanically be construed as a ground for its dismissal.
It is axiomatic that the high courts (bearing in mind the facts of each particular case) have a discretion whether to entertain a writ petition or not.

One of the self-imposed restrictions on the exercise of power under Article 226 that has evolved through judicial precedents is that the high courts should normally not entertain a writ petition, where an effective and efficacious alternative remedy is available.

At the same time, it must be remembered that mere availability of an alternative remedy of appeal or revision, which the party invoking the jurisdiction of the high court under Article 226 has not pursued, would not oust the jurisdiction of the high court and render a writ petition "not maintainable".

In a long line of decisions, this Court has made it clear that availability of an alternative remedy does not operate as an absolute bar to the "maintainability" of a writ petition and that the rule, which requires a party to pursue the alternative remedy provided The Branch Manager/Foreman vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96958256/
3 by a statute, is a rule of policy, convenience and discretion rather than a rule of law.

sentences.text: Though elementary, it needs to be restated that "entertainability" and "maintainability" of a writ petition are distinct concepts.
The fine but real distinction between the two ought not to be lost sight of.

The objection as to "maintainability"
goes to the root of the matter and if such objection were found to be of substance, the courts would be rendered incapable of even receiving the lis for adjudication.
On the other hand, the question of "entertainability" is entirely within the realm of discretion of the high courts, writ remedy being discretionary.

A writ petition despite being maintainable may not be entertained by a high court for very many reasons or relief could even be refused to the petitioner, despite setting up a sound legal point, if grant of the claimed relief would not further public interest.

Hence, dismissal of a writ petition by a high court on the ground that the petitioner has not availed the alternative remedy without, however, SRSJ examining whether an exceptional case has been made out for such entertainment would not be proper."

12. Thus, a perusal of the expression of the Hon'ble Apex Court makes it clear that mere availability of an alternative remedy is not a bar to maintain the writ petition, in a given case, if the petitioner satisfies the infringement of right.
In view of the same, this Court is of the opinion that writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is maintainable.
13. Case at hand, 2nd petitioner has been conducting chit business.

A perusal of the provisions of the Act makes it clear that jurisdictional Registrar is having over all control at the helm of affairs of Chit at every stage till the termination and even after termination till the disputes are resolved by way of arbitration.
Thus, jurisdictional Registrars, as per the provisions of the Act have been monitoring the affairs of every registered chit company.

Even before applying for sanction under Section 4 of the Act, the Foreman shall deposit in the name of Registrar an amount equal to 50% of gross chit amount in cash in appropriate bank and 50% in the form of SRSJ guarantee from appropriate bank.
Thus, the interest of each of the subscribers has been safe guarded.
14. A perusal of the complaint would manifest that signatures of complainant's husband were forged, and he did not join the chit.

The material papers, filed along with writ petition Exhibits P6 and P7, prima facie show that husband of defacto complainant joined as member of Chit Ref : LT 39TCR-27, value chit is Rs.5,00,000/- with a monthly subscription of Rs.10,000/- for 50 months.
Whether the signatures of husband of defacto complainant were forged or not is a matter to be investigated into.
Indeed, the 3rd respondent has been proceeding with investigation.
15. For the freezing of three accounts, referred to supra, as per Section 102 of Cr.P.C, there must be nexus with the offence alleged.

As seen from the averments in the writ affidavit there are total 1279 subscribers with 28 chit groups and husband of defacto complainant is one of the subscribers in one of the chit value of Rs.5,00,000/-.
The total amount freezed in 3 accounts referred to supra comes to Rs.1,49,38,313/-.
No complaint was made by any of the SRSJ members of other chit groups.

Thus,
freezing of three bank accounts, in the opinion of this Court, will cause prejudice to subscribers of 28 chit groups.
Making allegations simplicitor for the purpose of taking aid of Section 102 of Cr.P.C is not sufficient and proper.

It must be shown that allegation is found on such material so as to at The Branch Manager/Foreman vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96958256/

sentences.text: After completion of investigation, the true facts will come to light.
However, freezing of 3 accounts, at this stage, will cause irreparable loss and hardship.
The loss caused to the petitioners will not be compensated for at a later point in time.
16. Registration of the Chit itself with Registrar, the petitioners made out prima facie case.
One of chit subscribers' wife, among 1279 subscribers, made a complaint about forgery of signature of her husband.
In that connection freezing the three accounts of petitioners which involved the business transactions of others will cause irreparable loss which cannot be compensated at a later point in time.
Thus, this court is of the opinion that balance of convenience is in SRSJ favour of petitioners for grant of interim relief.
Thus, freezing of three accounts, referred to supra, needs to be suspended for the time being till a further decision in the writ petition and the counter affidavit to be filed by the respondents.

Though, the learned special government pleader would contend that the main relief and interim relief sought for in the writ petition are one and the same and hence interim relief cannot be granted at this stage, in the facts and circumstances of this case, unless interim order is granted it will cause irreparable loss to the petitioners.
17.
In view of discussion supra, the notice, under Section 102 Cr.P.C., issued by the 3rd respondent to freeze three accounts, referred to supra, is suspended pending further orders.

The respondents 4 and 5 shall defreeze the accounts of petitioners Margadarsi Chit Funds Private Limited, Chirala Branch vide Account Nos.917020029774550, 917020029775126 and 917020029775142 of Axis Bank, Chirala Branch forthwith.
However, this order will not come in the way of the 3rd respondent in proceeding with its investigation in connection with Crime No.283 of 2023 of Chirala I Town Police Station.
SRSJ 18. List the I.A.No.1 of 2023 after Dussehra Vacation, 2023.
